{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS: "can proposed ideas (like those from brainstorm) form a graph? looking at any idea individually may give you an incomplete picture. for example, we talked about black-boxes, systems engineering, functional allocation, and a few other inter-related ideas that paint a bigger, more holistic picture about what I'm trying to link together. or when my brother mentioned that sometimes he just wants to jot down ideas for a project over time. bottomline, does reflow2 link ideas/concepts or does it rely on the agent to do this?"

=== THE ANSWER, MEASURED 2026-08-21 RATHER THAN ESTIMATED ===

    145  idea-Decisions (dec:idea-*), of which 123 still proposed
     12  edges joining any TWO of them
     68  whose ONLY edge is AUTHORED_BY — they connect to their author and to nothing else
      8  with no edges at all

And the shape of what an idea IS connected to, across the whole population:
    134  AUTHORED_BY -> Contributor
     20  GOVERNED_BY -> Decision
     19  CONTRADICTS -> Decision
     13  DEPENDS_ON  -> Decision

⇒ THE MOST COMMON EDGE ON AN IDEA IS ITS AUTHOR. **The design records WHO had an idea far more reliably than WHAT IT RELATES TO.** Roughly half the idea population is an island that says 'Anthony thought this' and nothing further.

⭐ SO: REFLOW2 DOES NOT LINK IDEAS. IT RELIES ENTIRELY ON THE AGENT, AND THE AGENT MOSTLY DOES NOT. The evidence is this session: four of the twelve idea-to-idea edges in the entire graph were drawn BY HAND in one hour, only because Anthony asked for them in as many words. Every brainstorm before that produced a node and no edges — including three captured the previous day by the same agent following the same skill, which instructs recording the idea and says nothing about connecting it to its neighbours.

=== WHY IT MATTERS, IN HIS OWN CASE ===

Four nodes carry one argument between them and none of them says so on its own: allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment (accepted), what-watches-for-the-moment-to-arrive, the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph, and is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams. Read singly, each is a reasonable question. Read together they are one position about WHEN and ON WHAT BASIS a boundary gets drawn. A reader meeting any one of them alone gets an incomplete picture — which is exactly what he said.

AND HIS BROTHER'S CASE IS THE SAME SHAPE AT A DIFFERENT TIMESCALE: `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design) presumes the accretion can later be READ AS A WHOLE. Ideas jotted over months with no edges between them do not accrete into anything; they pile.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

  (a) THE STATUS QUO — the agent draws edges when it thinks to. Measured rate: 12 edges across 145 ideas, and a third of those in the hour after being asked. This is the option that produced the number.
  (b) THE BRAINSTORM SKILL REQUIRES NAMING A NEIGHBOUR. Cheap, needs no schema, and testable — the skill already makes the agent search before writing, so the near-matches are IN HAND at the moment of capture and are currently used only to avoid duplicates, then discarded. ⚠️ Risk: an edge drawn to satisfy an instruction is an asserted relationship nobody meant, which `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` forbids for exactly this reason.
  (c) A DETECTOR FOR THE ABSENCE — 'this idea shares vocabulary with N others and links to none'. It is the absence-shaped detector reflow2 structurally lacks (see fact:the-design-outward-blind-spot-appeared-in-three-independent-places), so building it would be the first of its kind rather than one more of many.
  (d) COMPUTE ADJACENCY, DO NOT STORE IT. `search_design` already ranks by BM25 over every node's text, so 'ideas near this one' is answerable TODAY as a READ without asserting any edge. Respects the no-fabrication rule completely: it SHOWS adjacency rather than CLAIMING a relationship. ⚠️ And its limit is the whole point — a similarity score cannot carry WHY two ideas are related, and the why is the content. The four edges drawn today each carry a note like 'option (b) here would be this one's stated trigger'; no ranking function produces that sentence.
  (e) DO NOTHING. Honest, and its cost is the measurement above.

=== COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE RATHER THAN AGAINST ===

An idea graph could be worse than an idea list. Edges between musings are cheap to draw and expensive to trust: two ideas mentioning 'allocation' are not thereby related, and a densely-linked pile of half-formed thoughts reads as a structure when it is a word cloud. This project has twice retired metric-driven verdicts that fired on correct architecture; a similarity-driven idea graph is the same hazard one level up. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE EDGE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP CARRIES A REASON — which is an argument for (b) or (d) over (c), and against any automatic drawing.
